questions.q: An auditor asks what a security group allowed on a specific date three months ago. Which service and feature answers this directly?

options.t: AWS Config configuration timeline or GetResourceConfigHistory
options.why: Right: Config stores point-in-time configuration items for each resource.
Wrong: it shows who called which API, not the full resource configuration at a date.
Wrong: it queries log data, not resource configuration.
Wrong: it detects threats and does not keep configuration history.

questions.explain: Config answers what the resource looked like and when it changed.
questions.remember: What a resource looked like at a past time → Config history. Who called the API → CloudTrail.
variants: The question is who opened the port → the Config item links the CloudTrail event ID, then use CloudTrail.
The question is whether the resource is compliant → Config rules.

questions.q: A security team must find all unencrypted EBS volumes across 40 accounts and several Regions, using the current configuration. What is the best approach?

options.t: An aggregator plus an advanced query
options.why: Right: advanced queries (SelectAggregateResourceConfig) run across accounts and Regions from an aggregator.

options.t: An advanced query in each account's console
options.why: Wrong: it works but is manual and not centralized.
Wrong: it queries API activity, not current resource state.

options.t: Athena over config history files only
options.why: Wrong: heavier, and not needed for a current-state question.

questions.explain: Aggregator queries give a central current-state view.
questions.remember: Current-state question across accounts → aggregator + advanced query. Past state → history/timeline/S3 + Athena.
variants: You need history over years → history files in S3 queried with Athena.
You need to deploy rules to all accounts → organization rules or conformance packs, not an aggregator.

questions.q: Config bills are high after turning on recording for all resource types. Some resources, like network interfaces, change constantly and per-change history is not needed. What should be done?

options.t: Use daily recording for the noisy types, or exclude them
options.why: Right: continuous recording bills per configuration item, daily gives at most one per resource per day.
Wrong: it only stops delivery to S3 and does not fix recording costs.
Wrong: S3 storage is a small part of the cost; CIs drive it.

options.t: Switch the rules to hybrid trigger
options.why: Wrong: this affects rule evaluation, not CI count.

questions.explain: Cost follows the number of CIs recorded.
questions.remember: High Config cost from noisy resources → record only needed types, exclude noisy ones, or record them daily.
variants: Cost comes from too many periodic rules → reduce frequency or use configuration-change triggers.
Many rules over many resources → scope rules by tag or resource type.

questions.q: A company wants an S3 bucket that becomes public to be fixed automatically. Which design fits?

options.t: A Config rule such as s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited with automatic remediation using an SSM Automation runbook
options.why: Right: Config detects the NON_COMPLIANT resource and runs the runbook.

options.t: A conformance pack with no remediation
options.why: Wrong: it detects but does not fix.

options.t: An aggregator in the security account
options.why: Wrong: it is a read-only view and cannot change resources.
Wrong: it detects unusual API activity but does not remediate.

questions.explain: Detect with a rule, fix with an SSM Automation runbook.
questions.remember: Auto-fix a non-compliant resource → Config rule + remediation action (SSM Automation, with an AutomationAssumeRole).
variants: The fix could break production → use manual remediation with an approval step.
You need custom fix logic → your own SSM runbook, or Lambda through EventBridge.

questions.q: A company must block non-compliant resources before they are deployed through CloudFormation. Which Config capability applies?

options.t: Proactive evaluation mode, for example with CloudFormation Hooks
options.why: Right: proactive rules check configuration before deployment.
Wrong: it evaluates resources that already exist.
Wrong: it only allows data sharing to an aggregator.
Wrong: it is a picture of existing resources.

questions.remember: Check before deploy → proactive rules or Hooks. Check after deploy → detective rules. Block actions outright → SCPs.
variants: You must stop any user from performing an action → SCP or IAM (preventive).
Existing resources must be checked → detective mode.

questions.q: A company needs CIS and PCI DSS checks, with remediation, deployed the same way to 50 accounts in an organization. Which option is best?

options.t: An organization conformance pack from a delegated administrator
options.why: Right: a pack bundles rules and remediation in one template and deploys to all accounts.
Wrong: it views data and does not deploy rules.

options.t: Individual rules created by hand in each account
options.why: Wrong: slow and hard to keep consistent.
Wrong: it is a data export, not governance.

questions.explain: Packs deploy rules and remediation as one unit.
questions.remember: Repeatable framework-aligned governance across accounts → organization conformance pack. Central view → aggregator.
variants: You only need a cross-account compliance dashboard → organization aggregator.
You need one rule deployed to all accounts → organization Config rule.

questions.q: A custom Config rule only needs to check that a resource property equals a required value. The team wants no code to maintain. Which type fits?

options.why: Right: Guard is a policy-as-code DSL over the configuration item and needs no Lambda.
Wrong: it works but needs code and permissions, better for complex logic.
Wrong: created by other services and cannot be edited.
Wrong: a pack is only a bundle of rules.

questions.remember: Simple check → Guard rule. Complex logic or calling other APIs → Lambda rule (PutEvaluations).
variants: The check must call another API → Lambda custom rule.
A prebuilt check exists → use a managed rule.

questions.q: A security team wants to make sure no one, including administrators, can stop the Config recorder or delete the delivery channel in member accounts. What should they use?

options.t: An SCP denying StopConfigurationRecorder, DeleteConfigurationRecorder and DeleteDeliveryChannel
options.why: Right: SCPs apply even to account administrators.

options.t: A Config rule that checks the recorder
options.why: Wrong: it detects but does not prevent.
Wrong: it protects delivered files, not the recorder.
Wrong: it is a read-only view.

questions.remember: Protect Config from being switched off → SCP deny on recorder and delivery channel actions.
variants: You need to be alerted when it is changed → EventBridge rule on the API call via CloudTrail.
Protect delivered data → versioning, Object Lock, locked-down log archive bucket.

questions.q: Security Hub controls show no data for some resource types. What is the most likely fix?

options.t: Enable the Config recorder for those resource types
options.why: Right: Security Hub controls rely on Config rules, which only evaluate recorded resources.
Wrong: retention does not affect evaluations.
Wrong: it does not make rules evaluate.
Wrong: it finds sensitive data and is unrelated to control evaluation.

questions.explain: No recording means no evaluation data.
questions.remember: A Config rule shows no data or INSUFFICIENT_DATA → check the resource type is recorded and the rule scope.
variants: Control Tower detective controls show not available → check recorder and Config service-linked rules in that Region.
An aggregator shows missing accounts → authorization not accepted or recorder off.

questions.q: An unencrypted RDS instance is found by the rds-storage-encrypted rule. Encryption cannot be added in place. What is the right response?

options.t: Mark NON_COMPLIANT, notify through EventBridge, and restore from an encrypted snapshot copy
options.why: Right: the fix is a restore, so alert a human.

options.t: Use automatic remediation to enable encryption on the instance
options.why: Wrong: encryption cannot be turned on for an existing unencrypted instance.
Wrong: this hides the problem.
Wrong: it only changes CI frequency.

questions.explain: Some fixes need rebuilds, so notify instead of auto-fixing.
questions.remember: Fix not possible in place → detect with a rule, notify via EventBridge/SNS, rebuild manually.
variants: The fix is a simple setting such as public access block → automatic remediation.
Compliance change must notify a team → EventBridge rule on Config Rules Compliance Change → SNS.
